messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: HIGH QUEUE ALERT for gpu-serving cluster-us-east-1. queue_length > 95th percentile for 3m, token-throttle spikes, 502s increasing. Pager: page to oncall.
incident-bot: incident created: INC-2026-349 - GPU queue growth + autoscaler stall. Assigned: Tim J. oncall. Use #inc-2951234567 for coordination.
Tim J.: I'm on it, grabbing logs and dashboard links. Any customer-facing impact yet?
Sally H.: Support seeing increased error rates for several customers, esp low-latency chat routes. Some customers hitting 429s. support ticket count +7 in last 15m.
Ravi K.: Pulling autoscaler logs — looks like scale operations are being rejected by rate-limiter: "scale_ops_quota_exceeded" from autoscaler-stepper. Happened at 2951234501.
Megan W.: Noted recent rollout 02:20 UTC: continuous-batching window changed from 150ms -> 650ms in rollout config v11. That increases batching latency and can lower effective throughput for short requests. Also prefix-cache-ttl was unintentionally set to 30s (was 5m). Might be causing a missstorm.
Tim J.: OK that aligns. Missed prefixes -> KV cache miss storm -> more GPU memory churn -> lower throughput -> queues grow. Autoscaler sees spike but hits rate cap and refuses to scale. Rough domino.
Infra Oncall: I can manually add capacity if we need to. What's the mitigation plan?
Ravi K.: Immediate actions I suggest: 1) pause rollout / rollback batch window to 150ms, 2) increase prefix-cache-ttl back to 5m, 3) bump autoscaler quota temporarily, 4) add 2 dedicated GPUs to pool as hotfix, 5) route non-prod/low-priority customers to CPU fallback.
Megan W.: Agree. Rolling back config now. Pushing v10 config for continuous-batching and prefix-cache TTL.
Megan W.: (after) Rolled back continuous-batching to 150ms and set prefix-cache-ttl=300s. Also pinned model variant to 1.4.
Tim J.: Executing manual scale up for pool redwood-gpu-prod-1: 
```
infractl pool scale --pool redwood-gpu-prod-1 --add-gpus 2 --reason "INC-2026-349 manual hotpatch"
```
Infra Oncall: Scale command accepted, provisioning GPUs (ETA ~4m).
Support Lead: I'm drafting a brief customer message for affected customers. No major data loss, degraded latency and 429s. Holding until we confirm mitigation improves metrics.
Ravi K.: Temporarily increased autoscaler rate limit on controller: set SCALE_OPS_ALLOWANCE=50 -> 200 for region us-east-1. Monitor closely.
Tim J.: Enabling safemode reroute for non-latency-sensitive product routes: set route override for embeddings/longform to route->cpu-fallback. Command: 
```
apictl routes update --service embeddings --route default --fallback cpu-fallback
```
Megan W.: CPU fallback enabled for embeddings and batch-embeddings.
Ravi K.: Observability: queue_length started trending down 2m after rollback, token-throttle % dropped from 23% -> 9% in next sample. Autoscaler accepted 2 scale ops and new nodes are joining.
pagerbot: Notification: new nodes joined redwood-gpu-prod-1 (gw-821, gw-822).
Sally H.: Support: error rate for impacted customers dropping, now stable at elevated but improving. Sending update to top 10 impacted customers.
Tim J.: Running quick smoke against chat route to verify tail latencies:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":5}' | jq '.latency'
```
Tim J.: tail latencies returned ~160ms (was 400-800ms). Good.
Ravi K.: Followups: need postmortem and rollback root cause. Short blameless notes: rollout introduced two risky param changes together (batch window + prefix-cache TTL) which interacted; autoscaler had defensive rate limit that prevented quick horizontal scale.
Support Lead: I've sent status update to customers affected: summary + timeline + ETA to full recovery (monitoring 30m).
Infra Oncall: New nodes stable, eviction churn reduced. Monitoring GPU mem alloc patterns — prefixcache hit-rate jumped from 12% -> 78% after TTL rollback.
Megan W.: Filing immediate rollback PR to forbid simultaneous changes of continuous-batching and prefix-cache settings in the same rollout.
Tim J.: On-call handoff: I'm paged for 35m total. After that I'll hand to Ravi for deeper analysis and postmortem. @Ravi K. confirm you'll take handoff?
Ravi K.: I'll take the handoff, thanks. Will start collecting traces, config diffs, and autoscaler telemetry.
incident-bot: oncall-handoff recorded: from Tim J. -> Ravi K. at 2951236700.
Megan W.: Quick note for postmortem: include perfbench with v11 config to reproduce reduced throughput with short-latency traffic; attempt to replay prefix-cache TTL miss pattern.
Sally H.: Closing loop with support: customers acknowledged update, some asked for detailed postmortem. We'll queue follow-up once postmortem is done.
Tim J.: Summary: mitigation done — rollback configs + prefix-cache TTL bump + manual scale + autoscaler quota bump + safemode reroute. Queue stabilized and tail latencies improved. Assigning postmortem to Eng Platform + Runtime + SRE.
Ravi K.: I'll own the postmortem write-up and will tag runtime and eng-platform. Preliminary action items: stricter rollout checks, autoscaler dynamic quota, canary for cache-ttl changes.
Sally H.: Thanks team. Marking incident as 'mitigated' in the incident tracker. Will update Support when postmortem is ready. :thumbsup:
Support Lead: Adding affected tickets to the incident bundle and notifying account leads.
Megan W.: Adding follow-up runbook item: block prefix-cache-ttl changes without perfbench and traffic-profiles.
Tim J.: Closing coordination here. If anything regresses reopen. Good job.
Ravi K.: I'll post initial postmortem draft in #postmortems within 24h.
incident-bot: Incident status changed: MITIGATED at 2951236840."
